data.narrative:
Svante, a Series E climate and energy technology company founded by Brett Henkel, has raised $318M to date. The valuation landscape comprises a fragmented peer set: one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private firms operating in Climate & Energy, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The peer-median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrowly-filtered comparables—only one same-stage peer was identified, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical validity. Consequently, analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E advancement to the $318M total raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $445M.

The triangulation analysis supports a range of $378M (low) to $512M (high), with a median of $445M. This single-method result carries meaningful uncertainty. Key limitations include the thinly-populated peer universe within Climate & Energy at comparable stages and valuations, and reliance on a raised-capital proxy rather than direct pre-money or post-money transaction data. Resolution of this uncertainty would require either expanded access to recent Climate & Energy fundraising at similar stages or additional transaction evidence from the identified peer set.
